paper_metadata.title: Quantum Circuit-Based Adaptation for Credit Risk Analysis

summary: The paper experimentally implements hardware‑aware variational circuits for Gaussian distribution loading (2‑ and 3‑qubit registers) and a 3‑qubit Gaussian Conditional Independence (GCI) credit‑risk circuit on a 17‑qubit QuantWare Contralto‑D superconducting processor. Optimal angles (e.g., θ0=90°, θ1=237° for the 2‑qubit case and θ0=90°, θ1=212.5°, θ2=104.5° for the 3‑qubit case) were tuned directly on hardware, and the resulting probability distributions reproduce a classical credit‑risk CDF with ~5% experimental error, placing the 95% VaR at the same loss level (L=1000) as the classical model.

experiments.description: Hardware-aware variational loading of a discrete 2-qubit Gaussian distribution for credit-risk latent factor modeling on a superconducting QPU, using the D3-C4 pair.

algorithm.ansatz: 2-qubit hardware-efficient ansatz with Ry on each qubit followed by CNOT
algorithm.convergence_criteria: not explicitly stated; angles selected by variational optimization and hardware sweep
algorithm.parameter_initialization: classically optimized angles from target-histogram training; then hardware sweep around the optimized region

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 2 qubits encode a 4-point discretized latent normal variable z; Ry angles shape the probability distribution over basis states
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize squared distance between measured basis-state probabilities p_b(θ) and target discrete Gaussian histogram p*_b

problem_instance.description: Prepare a discrete standard normal distribution over a 2-qubit register for latent-factor loading in credit-risk analysis
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: target histogram constructed by mapping basis indices to grid points in [-zmax,zmax] and fitting a discrete Gaussian
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: hardware sweep over θ1; comparison to Gaussian fit; 100 repeated measurements for error bars

hardware.framework: Quantify (Qblox control stack); Qiskit used only for circuit transpilation experiments
hardware.transpilation_target: hardware-aware transpilation to the Contralto-D coupling map; native CZ via SNZ pulses

noise_model.noise_type: NISQ superconducting hardware noise / SPAM / depolarizing and phase errors
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: none; hardware-aware calibration and counter-phase tuning

implementation_details.mitigation_details: No readout error mitigation; calibration via Rabi, Ramsey, AllXY, Motzoi, RB/IRB; counter-phase Z used in CNOT decomposition on some pairs
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: classical target-histogram construction and variational angle search
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: histogram comparison to Gaussian fit and error-bar estimation

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or empirical speedup claim is made; the paper reports hardware-aware distribution loading and calibration only.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed; experiment only demonstrates Gaussian distribution loading on a 2‑qubit register.
limiting_factors: No runtime or scaling comparison with classical distribution sampling
Variational parameter sweep performed manually on hardware
Noise and SPAM errors affect histogram symmetry

notes: circuit depth not explicitly reported; inferred as shallow 1-entangler ansatz from circuit description.
speedup order not analyzed in paper; no asymptotic advantage claim.
The authors explicitly present the experiment as a proof‑of‑concept for hardware‑aware distribution loading rather than a performance comparison against classical sampling.

experiments.description: Hardware-aware variational loading of a discrete 3-qubit Gaussian distribution for credit-risk latent factor modeling on a superconducting QPU, using the D3-A6-C4 triplet.

algorithm.ansatz: 3-qubit hardware-efficient ansatz with Ry on each qubit and two entanglers (CNOT0,1 and CNOT0,2)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: not explicitly stated; angles selected by variational optimization and hardware sweep
algorithm.parameter_initialization: classically optimized angles from target-histogram training; then hardware sweep around the optimized region

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 3 qubits encode an 8-point discretized latent normal variable z; Ry angles and entanglers shape the probability distribution over basis states
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize squared distance between measured basis-state probabilities p_b(θ) and target discrete Gaussian histogram p*_b

problem_instance.description: Prepare a discrete standard normal distribution over a 3-qubit register for latent-factor loading in credit-risk analysis
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: target histogram constructed by mapping basis indices to grid points in [-zmax,zmax] and fitting a discrete Gaussian
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: hardware sweep over θ1 and θ2; comparison to Gaussian fit; 100 repeated measurements for error bars

hardware.transpilation_target: hardware-aware transpilation to the Contralto-D coupling map; native CZ via SNZ pulses

noise_model.noise_type: NISQ superconducting hardware noise / SPAM / depolarizing and phase errors
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: none; hardware-aware calibration and counter-phase tuning

implementation_details.mitigation_details: No readout error mitigation; calibration via Rabi, Ramsey, AllXY, Motzoi, RB/IRB; counter-phase Z used in CNOT decomposition on some pairs
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: classical target-histogram construction and variational angle search
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: histogram comparison to Gaussian fit and error-bar estimation

speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim is made; the experiment demonstrates hardware-aware variational loading and scaling to 3 qubits.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed; experiment extends Gaussian loader to 3 qubits (8 basis states).
limiting_factors: Distribution preparation relies on hardware tuning of angles
Noise limits symmetry of prepared distribution

notes: circuit depth not explicitly reported; inferred as shallow 3-qubit ansatz with two entanglers from circuit description.
speedup order not analyzed in paper; no asymptotic advantage claim.
The experiment evaluates circuit output histograms and agreement with Gaussian targets but does not benchmark computational advantage.

experiments.description: Hardware-aware implementation of the one-factor Gaussian Conditional Independence (GCI) credit-risk circuit on a superconducting QPU, using a transpiled 3-qubit register and hardware-tuned rotation angles.

algorithm.variant: QAE-inspired GCI state-preparation subcircuit / hardware-ready transpiled credit-risk circuit
algorithm.ansatz: transpiled 3-qubit circuit with Ry and Rz rotations plus Hadamard/CZ-based CNOT decompositions
algorithm.optimizer: Adam and SABRE-based transpilation; hardware-level variational tuning of rotation angles
algorithm.convergence_criteria: not explicitly stated; tuned to match experimental CDF/VaR behavior
algorithm.parameter_initialization: angles derived from classical/noiseless model and then re-optimized on hardware; SABRE initial mapping for transpilation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 3 qubits: 2-qubit Gaussian latent-factor loader plus 1 asset qubit; measured bitstrings are postprocessed into latent-factor and default indicators
problem_formulation.objective_function: estimate credit-risk loss distribution / CDF and 95% VaR for a one-factor GCI model
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: hardware-aware transpilation; replacement of a transpiled subcircuit with an experimentally calibrated Gaussian-loading subcircuit; counter-phase Rz inserted in CNOT decomposition

problem_instance.description: One-asset, one-latent-factor credit-risk analysis instance under the Gaussian conditional-independence model

dataset_specification.description: latent Z ~ N(0,1), p0 = 0.25, rho = 0.027, 95% VaR at loss L=1000

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: bitstrings split into latent-variable bits and default bits; latent bits converted to integer index; default bits used to accumulate scenario losses and CDF
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: compare simulated transpiled circuit, hardware-ready transpiled circuit, and experimental output; evaluate CDF and VaR agreement

hardware.framework: Quantify (Qblox control stack); Qiskit used for transpilation pipeline
hardware.transpilation_target: Qiskit preset pass manager with SABRE routing on Contralto-D; native CZ via SNZ pulses

noise_model.noise_type: NISQ superconducting hardware noise / SPAM / depolarizing and phase errors
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: none; hardware-aware transpilation, counter-phase compensation, and in-situ variational tuning

implementation_details.mitigation_details: Qiskit preset pass manager, SABRE mapping, synthesis-based approximation budget, replacement of a uniform subcircuit with calibrated Gaussian loader, counter-phase Rz in CNOT decomposition
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: CDF construction from measured bitstrings; loss aggregation and VaR extraction
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compare experimental and simulated CDFs; compute 95% VaR and total-loss distribution

classical_baselines.method_name: simulated hardware-ready transpiled quantum circuit (Fig. S15)

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not claim a computational speedup; it reports agreement of experimental CDF/VaR with simulated baselines after hardware-aware transpilation.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Full credit‑risk quantum amplitude estimation (QAE) pipeline with large qubit registers and fault‑tolerant execution; not implemented here.
limiting_factors: Only a 3‑qubit subcircuit of the CRA algorithm implemented
No amplitude estimation iterations or Grover amplification executed
Output compared only at two loss grid points
NISQ noise and hardware‑specific tuning dominate performance
Potential quadratic speedup of QAE insufficient under Hoefler constant‑factor analysis

notes: The paper frames the GCI circuit as QAE-based, but the reported experiment is a hardware-ready state-preparation/transpilation study rather than a full amplitude-estimation loop; algorithm.family mapped to amplitude-estimation because the use case is explicitly QAE-based credit-risk analysis.
circuit depth not explicitly reported; inferred from the transpiled 3-qubit circuit structure.
speedup order not analyzed in paper; no asymptotic advantage claim.
The paper reports that the quantum and classical CDF outputs are 'indistinguishable' for the toy instance, indicating parity rather than advantage.
